Messiah's Kingdom; Desolations, to Be Succeeded by Lasting Peace, the Spirit Having Been Poured Out.</title> <div sID="gen14894" type="x-p"/> The times of purity and happiness which shall follow the defeat of the enemies of Jehovah's people (<reference osisRef="Isa.32.1-Isa.32.8">Is 32:1-8</reference>). The period of wrath before that happy state (<reference osisRef="Isa.32.9-Isa.32.14">Is 32:9-14</reference>). The assurance of the final prosperity of the Church is repeated (<reference osisRef="Isa.32.15-Isa.32.20">Is 32:15-20</reference>).<div eID="gen14894" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14895" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8896"/><hi type="bold">1. king--</hi>not Hezekiah, who was already on the throne, whereas a future time is contemplated. If he be meant at all, it can only be as a type of Messiah the King, to whom alone the language is fully applicable (<reference osisRef="Hos.3.5">Ho 3:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.9.9">Zec 9:9</reference>; see on <reference osisRef="Isa.11.3-Isa.11.5">Is 11:3-5</reference>). The kingdom shall be transferred from the world kings, who have exercised their power against God, instead of for God, to the rightful King of kings (<reference osisRef="Ezek.21.27">Eze 21:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.7.13">Da 7:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Dan.7.14">14</reference>).<div eID="gen14895" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14896" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">princes--</hi>subordinate; referring to all in authority under Christ in the coming kingdom on earth, for example, the apostles, &c. (<reference osisRef="Luke.22.30">Lu 22:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.6.2">1Co 6:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Tim.2.12">2Ti 2:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.2.26">Re 2:26</reference>, 27; 3:21). <div eID="gen14896" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 32 Is 32:1-20 . Messiah's Kingdom; Desolations, to Be Succeeded by Lasting Peace, the Spirit Having Been Poured Out. The times of purity and happiness which shall follow the defeat of the enemies of Jehovah's people ( Is 32:1-8 ). The period of wrath before that happy state ( Is 32:9-14 ). The assurance of the final prosperity of the Church is repeated ( Is 32:15-20 ). 1. king-- not Hezekiah, who was already on the throne, whereas a future time is contemplated. If he be meant at all, it can only be as a type of Messiah the King, to whom alone the language is fully applicable ( Ho 3:5 ; Zec 9:9 ; see on Is 11:3-5 ). The kingdom shall be transferred from the world kings, who have exercised their power against God, instead of for God, to the rightful King of kings ( Eze 21:27 ; Da 7:13 , 14 ). princes-- subordinate; referring to all in authority under Christ in the coming kingdom on earth, for example, the apostles, &c. ( Lu 22:30 ; 1Co 6:2 ; 2Ti 2:12 ; Re 2:26 , 27; 3:21).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8899"/><div sID="gen14901" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8899"/><hi type="bold">4. rash--</hi>rather, "the hasty"; contrast "shall not make haste" (<reference osisRef="Isa.28.16">Is 28:16</reference>); the reckless who will not take time to weigh religious truth aright. Or else, the well-instructed [Horsley].<div eID="gen14901" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14902" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">stammers--</hi>those who speak confusedly on divine things (compare <reference osisRef="Exod.4.10-Exod.4.12">Ex 4:10-12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.1.6">Jr 1:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.10.19">Mt 10:19</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.10.20">20</reference>). Or, rather, those drunken scorners who in stammering style imitated Isaiah's warnings to mock them [Maurer] (<reference osisRef="Isa.28.7-Isa.11.13">Is 28:7-11, 13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.14.22">14, 22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.29.20">29:20</reference>); in this view, translate, "speak uprightly" (agreeably to the divine law); not as English Version, referring to the distinctness of articulation, "plainly." <div eID="gen14902" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 4. rash-- rather, "the hasty"; contrast "shall not make haste" ( Is 28:16 ); the reckless who will not take time to weigh religious truth aright. Or else, the well-instructed [Horsley]. stammers-- those who speak confusedly on divine things (compare Ex 4:10-12 ; Jr 1:6 ; Mt 10:19 , 20 ). Or, rather, those drunken scorners who in stammering style imitated Isaiah's warnings to mock them [Maurer] ( Is 28:7-11, 13 , 14, 22 ; 29:20 ); in this view, translate, "speak uprightly" (agreeably to the divine law); not as English Version, referring to the distinctness of articulation, "plainly."

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8904"/><div sID="gen14916" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8904"/><hi type="bold">9-20. Address to the women of Jerusalem who troubled themselves little about the political signs of the times, but lived a life of self-indulgence (<reference osisRef="Isa.3.16-Isa.3.23">Is 3:16-23</reference>); the failure of food through the devastations of the enemy is here foretold, being what was most likely to affect them as mothers of families, heretofore accustomed to every luxury. Vitringa understands "women--</hi>daughters" as the cities and villages of Judea (<reference osisRef="Ezek.16.1-Ezek.16.63">Eze 16:1-63</reference>). See <reference osisRef="Amos.6.1">Am 6:1</reference>. <div eID="gen14916" type="x-p"/>
